title: Camera Trails, Trig Combs, Diffusion Type, Dust & Compare
description: Five live drops: a scroll-driven SVG flyover camera, a trigonometric honeycomb grid, an AI-diffusion-style text decode, a precomputed-noise dust cursor, and a clip-path comparison slider.

drops.title: Scroll-Driven Path Camera
drops.description: An SVG route draws itself stroke-by-stroke as you scroll, while an inverse-transform camera pans and zooms to follow it.
drops.concept: As scroll progress advances, a path's stroke-dashoffset scrubs open while getPointAtLength() finds the exact point the line has reached. Applying the negative of that point as a transform to a parent group keeps it centered — the camera never moves, the world moves around it — producing a cinematic flyover with zero animation library.
drops.source: Codrops tutorial by Surya Aditya, "Building an Infinite GSAP Scroll Gallery" concept family — specifically "Creating Scroll-Driven SVG Map Animations with GSAP"

interaction.mouse: Scroll the page to fly the route
interaction.click: Tune zoom range, smoothing and route width in the panel

drops.title: Honeycomb Trig Grid
drops.description: A true tessellating hexagon gallery sized entirely by CSS trigonometry — no hardcoded ratio hack, no media queries.
drops.concept: CSS trig functions reaching full Baseline support let aspect-ratio: cos(30deg) replace the old memorized 1.1547 hexagon height constant. One --s custom property drives every hex's size, gap and overlap via calc(), so the honeycomb reflows continuously at any viewport width with zero breakpoints.
drops.source: Temani Afif — CSS-Tricks, "Responsive Hexagon Grid Using Modern CSS"

interaction.mouse: Hover a cell to reveal its description
interaction.click: Tune cell size, row overlap and flip flat/pointy-top orientation
interaction.touch: Tap a cell; resize the window to see it reflow

drops.title: Diffusion Decode Text
drops.description: Text renders like an AI image generator decoding a prompt — random glyph noise crystallizes into real words.
drops.concept: Each character starts as a random glyph with two independently-randomized RGB ghost trails behind it (feMorphology-free, pure pseudo-element + mix-blend-mode: screen). A per-character settle probability ramps with global progress, so words resolve unevenly rather than left-to-right, then hold, re-noise, and cycle to the next word — complete with a sampler chip and t-step readout.
drops.source: CodeFronts — "16 CSS Glitch Text Effects" collection, Demo #16 "Diffusion Decode Glitch Text"

interaction.click: Tune decode time, hold time and ghost intensity in the panel

drops.title: Precomputed Noise Dust Cursor
drops.description: A gritty dust trail flickers under the cursor by cycling through pre-baked noise frames instead of computing particle noise every frame.
drops.concept: Cursor position is read every animation frame for smooth tracking, but the dust texture itself only advances through a small library of precomputed noise frames a few times per second on its own independent clock. That mismatch — smooth motion, stepped texture — is what reads as gritty dust instead of a smooth CG blob, and it's cheaper than recalculating noise every frame.
drops.source: Robert Aperios / Codrops — "Run Rob Run: Building a Music-Reactive Goo with Three.js and WebGPU" (dust texture technique)

interaction.mouse: Move the cursor to leave a dust trail
interaction.click: Switch presets or tune flicker speed, brush radius and frame count
interaction.touch: Drag a finger across the screen

drops.title: Clip-Path Compare Slider
drops.description: A before/after image reveal that's a real accessible role="slider" control, driven entirely by clip-path: inset().
drops.concept: Instead of the classic width/overflow reveal, the top layer is clipped with clip-path: inset() — a GPU-composited property that needs no layout/paint on every drag frame. The handle is a genuinely focusable role="slider" element with pointer-capture dragging plus full arrow-key/Home/End keyboard support, turning a decades-old toy into a real accessible control.

interaction.mouse: Drag the handle, or click anywhere in the third demo to jump
interaction.click: Focus a slider and use arrow keys, Home or End
interaction.touch: Drag the handle with a finger
